business_context: The Gold Standard Execution KPI weights PACE (what the restaurant executed) and CSAT (what customers experienced) 50/50 for Taste and for Hospitality. Combining them is only defensible if we understand how they relate: whether they measure related things, where they diverge, and why.
decision_supported: Inform the GSE KPI design: whether a 50/50 PACE+CSAT index is coherent, which PACE scoring variant to use, and which time alignment and reporting grain make the two comparable. No immediate decision depends on it.

hypotheses.statement: Higher progressive PACE is associated with higher CSAT, for both Taste and Hospitality, within each market group.
hypotheses.rationale: The core question: do execution and perception move together at all?
hypotheses.support_criteria: Within-market-group r > 0 with a 95% CI excluding 0 and surviving FDR, at visit and restaurant-year grain.

pathway.purpose: Check ceiling effects and discreteness before correlating
Pooled visit-level association with cluster bootstrap CIs
Test whether pooling markets distorts the estimate
Restaurant-year association in Canada
Restaurant-year association in UK&I
Assumption-free significance, shuffled within market group
Slope after market, visit type and month controls

hypotheses.statement: The association is strongest when CSAT is measured close to the visit date.
hypotheses.rationale: PACE scores a moment; CSAT spans a period. Misaligned windows dilute the relationship.
hypotheses.support_criteria: A window around the visit (pm7-pm60) has a higher r than the calendar-year window.

pathway.purpose: Correlation by CSAT window around the visit
How much of window CSAT is sampling noise

hypotheses.statement: Unannounced CFV visits track CSAT better than announced RGRV visits.
hypotheses.rationale: RGRV tests capability; CFV tests the everyday experience customers rate.
hypotheses.support_criteria: RGRV scores higher than CFV and CFV r with CSAT >= RGRV r.

pathway.purpose: Size of the announced-visit gap and which visit type tracks CSAT

hypotheses.statement: The Hospitality relationship differs by channel.
hypotheses.rationale: Drive Thru interactions are short and human; Mobile orders skip the order-taker.
hypotheses.support_criteria: Channel-specific r differs (Fisher z) and the channel-matched pairing is at least as strong as all-channel CSAT.

pathway.purpose: Correlation by CSAT channel and tested channel
Correlation by restaurant type and CSAT volume band
Which product, channel, or touchpoint tracks CSAT most

hypotheses.statement: Progressive scoring differentiates restaurants better than conservative scoring and tracks CSAT at least as well.
hypotheses.rationale: The brief asks to use progressive for statistics and compare it with conservative.
hypotheses.support_criteria: Progressive has more distinct values and fewer ties, and r with CSAT >= conservative r.

pathway.purpose: Spread, ties, rank agreement, and r for each variant
CSAT when a visit passes vs fails conservatively

hypotheses.statement: CSAT drops more steeply for the weakest executors (threshold).
hypotheses.rationale: Customers may tolerate small lapses but react to poor execution.
hypotheses.support_criteria: Binned means and LOWESS show a steeper slope at low PACE, and a breakpoint model beats linear.

pathway.purpose: Mean CSAT by PACE band
Shape of the relationship
Locate a threshold

hypotheses.statement: Taste and Hospitality share a common 'well-run restaurant' factor, so the indexes overlap.
hypotheses.rationale: If both sides are driven by one factor, the 50/50 Taste/Hospitality split double counts it.
hypotheses.support_criteria: Cross-measure correlations approach same-measure ones, and shared variance is large in commonality analysis.

pathway.purpose: Same vs cross correlations
Unique vs shared variance
Which side really drives the GSE KPI ranking

hypotheses.statement: PACE and CSAT agree on which restaurants are best and worst.
hypotheses.rationale: A combined KPI is used to rank restaurants; agreement matters more than r.
hypotheses.support_criteria: Top and bottom quintile overlap well above 20% chance within market group.

pathway.purpose: Quintile overlap and tertile kappa
Size and profile of divergent quadrants
Stable restaurant differences vs good and bad days
FDR correction across every test in the run (run last)

threats: Market confounding: UK&I and Canada may differ in survey culture.
Only 3-5 PACE visits per restaurant per year.
out_of_scope: Causal effect of PACE on CSAT
Individual restaurant rankings for performance management
